messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course Summary:

Admission Date: [DATE]
Discharge Date: [DATE]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The 54-year-old male was admitted with a diagnosis of left hemisphere ischemic stroke. The patient had significant muscle atrophy resulting in limited voluntary motion in the arm and hand and severe impairment as indicated by the patient's Chedoke-McMaster Stroke Assessment hand score of 2. The patient did not exhibit any cognitive impairments.

Treatment:
The patient underwent a comprehensive treatment plan during their stay at the hospital. The treatment plan included rehabilitation sessions aimed at improving muscle strength and voluntary motion in the arm and hand. 

Outcome:
The patient's treatment plan resulted in gradual improvement in muscle strength and voluntary motion in the arm and hand. At the time of discharge, the patient's average ratio of maximum finger forces between hands was 0.076. Further follow-up sessions are recommended for continued improvement.

Follow-Up:
The patient was discharged with a comprehensive follow-up plan. The patient's progress will be monitored by the treating physician.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is the left hemisphere ischaemic stroke, i.e. cerebral infarction, which is chapter I. The care was rehabilitation for the resulting arm and hand weakness, but under ICD-10-AM rehabilitation conventions the underlying condition is the principal diagnosis and the rehabilitation code (Z50) is additional. This assumes the stroke is still current in this continued episode rather than coded as a late effect, so the category is I63.

CODE: I63
